hint.p: Remember that the derivative of \cot x is -\csc^2(x)
Let u = \cot\mathopen{}\left(5x\right). Don't forget chain rule when you take the derivative.

solution.p: Let u=\cot\mathopen{}\left(5x\right). Then we take the derivative of both sides to get du = -5\csc^{2}\mathopen{}\left(5x\right) \, dx

You can do the next step in different ways, but one way is to solve for dx. Since du = -5\csc^{2}\mathopen{}\left(5x\right) \, dx, we divide over to get that dx=\frac{1}{-5\csc^{2}\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)} \, du Then we substitute back into the original integral. \int -6 \csc^2(5 x) e^{\cot(5 x)} \, dx = \int -6 \csc^2(5 x) e^{u} \frac{1}{-5\csc^{2}\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)} \, du Which simplifies to \int 1.2e^{u}du

Now, this is one of our basic integrals, and we can integrate it. Constants in front just stay multiplied so we get \int 1.2e^{u}du = 1.2e^{u}+C Finally, make sure you put it back in terms of the original variable, which in this case is 'x'. So we substitute back in for 'u', which was \cot\mathopen{}\left(5x\right). Thus the final answer to this integral is \int -6 \csc^2(5 x) e^{\cot(5 x)} \, dx = 1.2e^{\cot\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)}+C
